title: Build the note
scenario: Can the note be built from the magazine's letters, each used at most once?

intro.job: Can the note be built from the magazine's letters, each used at most once?

model_restatement: Check whether the magazine has enough of every letter the note needs, counting repeats.

clarify.question: Can a magazine letter be used twice?
clarify.answer: No — each magazine letter can be used at most once.

clarify.question: What should I print?
clarify.answer: True if the note can be built, otherwise False.

clarify_fallback: Good question — assume the simple case.
blueprint: Note and magazine come as a pair. Make a list of the magazine's letters. For each note letter: if it's in the list, take it out; if not, the note can't be built. Print the answer.

checkpoints.prompt: With the fix — after counting the whole magazine (iteration 4), what is left?

why_line: 'l' in magazine only asks whether there's AN 'l' — it's True both times, so the second 'l' gets waved through even though the magazine has just one.

explain.rule: 'in' checks the wallet has that coin — it doesn't take the coin out, so you can spend the same 'l' forever.
explain.bridge: So how could you keep track of how many of each letter are left to spend?

fix.rule: Count the magazine's letters, then spend one per note letter — a count of 0 means you're out.

walk.gloss: ...and count each letter into the wallet.
For each note letter: none left? Then the note can't be built; otherwise spend one.

contrast.right_note: is there one left to spend?

alternatives.note: Spend by removing from a list — the same idea, slower on long magazines.

hints: How many 'l's does the note need? How many does the magazine have?
Count the magazine's letters, then subtract one per note letter.

follow_up.prompt: New note: 'book' from the magazine 'bok' — can it be built?

checkpoint.prompt: With note 'book' and magazine 'bok', what gets printed?

follow_up.fix_hint: Nothing to change — the second 'o' finds the wallet empty.

one_liner: Being in the magazine once isn't enough — each letter can only be spent once.

The letters the note is missing

questions.prompt: With THIS pair, can the note be built? Work it out by hand.
The note needs two l's, and 'l' is in the magazine. Is that enough?

instinct.scaffold:
note, magazine = pair
ok = True

print(ok)
hints: Each magazine letter can be used once — so when you use one, take it away.
Put the magazine's letters in a list. For each note letter: if it's in the list, remove it; if not, set ok = False.

why.this_data: Your version searches the list for every note letter: 5 note letters × up to 4 magazine letters = up to 20 looks.
why.real_size: With a 10,000-letter note and a 100,000-letter magazine that's up to a billion looks. Let's tally the magazine once, then just look each letter up.

blocks.title: Tally the magazine
blocks.teaches: left[ch] = left.get(ch, 0) + 1 adds one to that letter's tally — starting from 0 the first time.

checkpoints.prompt: Iteration 2, after line 3: what is left?

blocks.title: Spend one
blocks.teaches: left[ch] -= 1 uses up one of that letter.

blocks.title: Any left?
blocks.teaches: left.get(ch, 0) == 0 asks 'none left?' — a letter that was never there counts as 0 too.

blocks.title: In isn't the same as left
blocks.teaches: 'in' asks 'is there one at all?' — not 'is there one left to spend?'. Spend from the tally, and 0 means you're out.

checkpoints.prompt: The magazine 'helo' has one l; the note needs two. What gets printed?

hints: Which loop fills the tally, and which one spends from it?
B1's line tallies — it belongs in the magazine loop, before anything is spent.
Order: B1's line in the magazine loop, then B4's lines in the note loop.
